headline: Contrast makes things visible—difference captures attention while sameness fades into background
universal_truth: Difference creates meaning; we understand things by what they're not
fun_facts: Your brain actively ignores constant stimuli—a watch on your wrist 'disappears' until it changes
Black text on white paper works because maximum contrast aids readability
Predators often have camouflage that breaks up their outline—reducing contrast to hide
discussion_questions: What contrasts in your environment do you notice most?
How do advertisers use contrast to capture attention?
What would help you stand out through contrast?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A red dot on a white page jumps out. That same red dot on a red page disappears. Nothing changed about the dot—only its context. Contrast is how we see, how we notice, how anything stands out from everything else.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Our brains are wired to detect difference. Sameness fades into background while contrast pops forward. Why did evolution build brains that notice difference more than similarity?

options.text: Differences signal change, and change often signals opportunity or threat—evolutionarily, noticing change kept us alive
options.response: Yes. A rustle in the grass (contrast with stillness) might be a predator. A bright berry (contrast with green) might be food. Brains that noticed contrast survived better.

options.text: Contrast is easier for the brain to process
options.response: Processing efficiency matters, but the survival value of detecting change is primary...

q1.title: Edge Detection
q1.script: Your visual system is built around edge detection—finding where one thing ends and another begins. Edges are contrasts. Without contrast, you'd see a uniform field with no objects. Contrast literally creates what you see.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Edge Detection"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Habituation
q2.script: Constant stimuli fade away. You stop feeling your clothes, hearing the hum of appliances, noticing familiar environments. The brain conserves resources by ignoring sameness. Only change—contrast over time—gets attention.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Designed Contrast
q3.script: Designers use contrast deliberately: bold headlines, color accents, white space. What you want noticed needs contrast. Standing out requires difference. In a world of sameness, distinction gets attention.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Difference creates meaning. Contrast teaches that we understand things by what they're not. If you want to be noticed, be different. If you want to hide, be the same.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 180—half a year of learning! 🎉 Tomorrow, we'll explore how hot and cold work. Until then, notice what contrasts catch your eye—and consider what makes you stand out.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Contrast Audit - Stand Out or Blend In
growTrack.activity: Consider where you want to stand out and where you want to blend in. What contrasts help you in your goals? What sameness works against you? Attention follows contrast—use it deliberately in communication, presentation, and positioning.
